newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM lashes own Finance Ministry over scandals.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM lashes own Finance Ministry over scandals.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, angered by a string of business scandals, lashed out at his own Finance Ministry Thursday for failing to head off at least one of them.

The wave of scandals has broken in the middle of a campaign by Hashimoto's government to clean up the country's business ethics ahead of "Big Bang" deregulation of its financial markets to make them globally competitive.

In an unusual public rebuke to the country's most powerful bureaucrats, Hashimoto took them to task for not knowing that the country's third-largest commercial bank, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, might be involved in questionable loans to a racketeer.
"It's not only a matter of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank. There must have been inspections by the Finance Ministry," Hashimoto told reporters.
He also did not spare top executives of the bank, decrying reports that they might resign over the affair as "sneaky."

"It's sneaky (for the DKB leadership) to step down to take the blame," Hashimoto said. "Their resigning does not settle the problem. They should face up to the case until investigations make headway."

Media reports have said DKB Chairman Tadashi Okuda, President Katsuhiko Kondo and other top executives are expected to quit over links to a scandal also involving the country's largest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co.

At the heart of the affair is the activities of a "sokaiya," or racketeer, who prosecutors suspect was given financial favours by both companies to stop him disrupting their shareholders' meetings by asking sensitive business questions.
Japan's Commercial Code bans companies from making such payments.
